function: Jointly optimizes BS power allocation, SIM phase shifts, and STAR-RIS transmission-reflection coefficients to maximize energy efficiency under per-user rate and CRB sensing constraints (pp. 1, 4).
system: 0.1 THz ISAC; 8-antenna ULA BS with stacked SIM (4 layers, 16 atoms); STAR-RIS, simultaneously transmitting and reflecting (25 elements, 5 sensors); 4 single-antenna users, 4 targets (pp. 2, 5).
method: Meta-reinforcement learning: soft actor-critic with MAML meta-training and meta-adaptation, plus a GAN in the critic modeling state-action value distributions (pp. 4-5).
data_channel: Simulated THz channel: ray-tracing Saleh-Valenzuela SIM-to-STAR-RIS model with spatial correlation, spreading and absorption path loss; users and targets placed randomly; no external dataset (pp. 3, 5).
test_conditions: Meta-training on tasks of user and target placements; adaptation to unseen ones claimed (pp. 4-5); reported: convergence and EE sweeps over CRB bound, power, SIM size, sensors (p. 5).
baselines: Learned only: Meta-SAC (the proposed method without GAN), SAC, and PPO; no non-learned baseline (p. 5).
metrics: Energy efficiency and training reward; sensing accuracy enters only through the CRB threshold, varied in Fig. 2(b) (p. 5).
complexity: Big-O expressions for GAN training, Meta-SAC training, and running mode, and their sum; no numerical operations count or runtime (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 3: "channel is characterized using a ray-tracing Saleh-Valenzuela". Not met: custom Saleh-Valenzuela THz channel with spreading and absorption path loss; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "achieves faster and smoother convergence than other DRL methods". Not met: adaptation to unseen environments is claimed (p. 4) but no result tests a trained model on a new placement or configuration; Fig. 2 shows convergence and EE sweeps only.
q3_support: p. 5: "we compare it with benchmark algorithms: Meta-SAC, SAC, and PPO". Not met: all three are learned (Meta-SAC is the method without the GAN), compared by reward convergence (Fig. 2a); no non-learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 5: "The complexity analysis of the proposed GAN-based Meta-SAC algorithm can be divided into three parts". Eqs. (11)-(13) give the order of complexity of training and running.
q5_support: p. 5: "Additional SIM parameters align with [3] and Meta-SAC training follows [18]". Not met: parameters are listed, but no code or data link and no public dataset; the channel is simulated (p. 3).
notes: Letter. Area 5 rather than 3: the learned Meta-SAC sets power, SIM phase shifts and STAR-RIS coefficients under a CRB sensing constraint, an ISAC beam and resource problem, and ISAC outranks area 3. Reviewer checks. (1) q2 is 0 because adaptation to unseen environments is claimed (p. 4: "enabling the agent to adapt quickly to unseen environments") but no test on new placements or configurations is reported; if Fig. 2(a) is read as meta-adaptation to new tasks, q2 could be 1. (2) q3 is 0 for lack of any non-learned baseline; Meta-SAC is an ablation of the proposed method. (3) q4 rests on the symbolic big-O formulas of Section III-C (p. 5); no numbers or runtime.
